extraction.name: HELVIPAD: A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation containing paired top-bottom 360° images with depth and disparity labels, collected in indoor and outdoor human environments and augmented with depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbiere, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig on a university campus, capturing indoor and outdoor scenes under diverse lighting and weather conditions. The rig used two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor. A central processor managed capture and synchronization. The dataset includes video sequences recorded between December 2023 and February 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection; Direct measurement; Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: LiDAR point clouds are sparse, so ground-truth depth labels cover only a fraction of pixels before depth completion. Occlusions were not explicitly handled. Some regions such as sky and ground were cropped out.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Paired equirectangular images from two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras and synchronized LiDAR point clouds from an Ouster OS1-64 sensor.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A fully automated depth completion pipeline was applied to LiDAR point clouds to increase label density. It temporally aggregated point clouds from four preceding and four succeeding frames, interpolated depth on spherical grid points using k-nearest neighbors, and filtered points with high uncertainty or insufficient nearby measurements before mapping them to images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images using optimized rotation and translation parameters. Depth values were converted to disparity values. Images and labels were cropped to remove unnecessary borders, and images were downsized from 1024 pixels width to 512 for training efficiency.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sequences were synchronized using a flash trigger and ROS timestamps; one out of every three camera frames was retained to match LiDAR frame rate. Sky and ground regions were cropped. The dataset was split into train-val and test sets with manual review to ensure no overlap of scenes or areas. Depth completion was used to create an augmented training set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations consist of depth and disparity labels derived from LiDAR point clouds projected onto equirectangular images. The projection was calibrated using manually selected corresponding 3D points and image points on a chessboard. No separate human labeling of semantic classes is described.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Projection accuracy was manually validated by selecting corresponding points and computing pixel-wise error. The average projection error was reported as 8.0 pixels overall. Depth completion quality was evaluated with train/test splits and metrics such as MAE, RMSE, MARE, IR, ARIP, and RLP.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Sparse original LiDAR labels; after depth completion, the labeled pixel ratio increased from about 12% to about 61% overall.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LiDAR-to-image projection pipeline; depth completion pipeline using spherical-grid interpolation and k-nearest neighbors; BFGS optimization for calibration; KISS-ICP for optional odometry-based temporal aggregation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Pedestrian presence/counts are recorded in the sequences; the dataset includes human environments and scenes with pedestrians, but no explicit personal attributes such as gender, age, or ethnicity are collected.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support robotic navigation and depth estimation in human environments, with potential relevance to autonomous systems operating in indoor and outdoor public spaces.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected on a university campus and emphasizes urban-like environments such as corridors, halls, roads, parking areas, pedestrian squares, and footpaths. It includes indoor, outdoor, and night outdoor scenes, but the paper notes that indoor-trained models generalize poorly to outdoor and night conditions, indicating scene imbalance effects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: LiDAR depth is sparse and less accurate at longer ranges; occlusions were not explicitly handled; temporal aggregation is limited for fast-moving objects like cars; the dataset is collected on a university campus, which may limit generalization to other environments; some benchmark metrics rely on sparse ground truth and augmented labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, testing, benchmarking, fine-tuning, and cross-scene/cross-dataset generalization evaluation for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation.
